newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials and techs slide, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials and techs slide, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: Stocks tumbled Friday, dragged lower by profit-taking in the red-hot technology sector.

The Dow Jones industrial average fell as much as 145 points but later recovered some ground and was off about 104 points, or 1.3 percent, at 7,916 in morning trading. The drop came two days after the Dow broke 8,000 for the first time.
The Nasdaq composite index, laden with tech stocks that have powered the broader market's recent rise, fell more sharply, losing 22.64 points, or 1.44 percent, to 1,546.21.
Tech stocks took a beating after Microsoft Corp. reported an 88 percent jump in earnings that some investors viewed as disappointing. Microsoft fell $6.75 to $142.75 on Nasdaq.

"The market is in general profit-taking mode in names which have done exceedingly well in recent weeks," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "It's volatile. When you have stocks which have gone up 10 points in a week, they will correct with equal velocity."
The drop came two days after the market rallied to push the Dow average of 30 blue-chips above 8,000 for the first time.
A mild drop in the bond market also gave stock investors an excuse to take profits and the expiration of stock options and index options contributed to price swings, investors said.
The 30-year Treasury fell 11/32, or $3.44 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.52 percent from 6.49 percent on Thursday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Microsoft said on Thursday that earnings jumped 88 percent to $1.05 billion, or 80 cents a share, in the latest quarter, reflecting surging sales of Windows and other computer software.

While the profits were a penny above Wall Street's average estimate of 79 cents a share, the stock fell since the company did not have a big "blowout" quarter as it did three months ago, when earnings beat estimates by 23 percent.
"Microsoft was the catalyst on the downside," Bleier said.
Other tech stocks also fell. Intel Corp. lost $1.375 to $86.44, Compaq Computer Corp. fell $3.19 to $128.875 and Hewlett-Packard Co. lost $1.375 to $65.125.

But International Business Machines Corp. rose after Merrill Lynch raised its price target on the stock to $150. IBM jumped $4.125 to $103.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Big Blue is due to report earnings on Monday.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 11.60 to 920.01.
The American Stock Exchange index fell 5.46 points to 631.88.
